title: Gutenberg's Bible
hookLine: a goldsmith's press in Mainz prints the Bible, and books start to get cheap

lines: A WHOLE BIBLE, PAGE BY PAGE.
cards: A tiny metal letter, the size of a fingernail, stands on its end. A capital I. Next to it, an n.

Then another, and another, until a whole line sits in a wooden frame, backward, like a word seen in a mirror. Ink goes over it, paper comes down, a screw turns, and the page comes up with the words the right way round.
Then the letters come apart and get set again for the next page. In a workshop in the German city of Mainz, a goldsmith named Johannes Gutenberg is doing this with the whole Bible.

teach.h: COPIED BY HAND, ONE AT A TIME.
teach.b: Before the press, every Bible in Europe was copied by hand, the way Thomas à Kempis copied at his desk. Every copy was its own work, and precious.

Gutenberg's idea was to make the letters movable: cast them in metal, line them up, print a page, then break them apart and use them again. His Bible was in Latin, the Bible the Western church read in worship.

Its Genesis begins with the words the King James Bible gives as: "In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth." The pages were made to look like the best handwritten books: two columns, dark, even letters.

Copies were often finished by hand, with red headings and painted capitals, so no two look quite the same. Then other presses followed, in other cities. Books got cheaper, and more people could own one.
Later, reformers would print the Bible in German and English, in the languages people spoke at home, and tracts and sermons traveled fast.
Christians argued, sometimes fiercely, over what all those readers should do with what they read. But the change underneath was simple.

teach.h: A LAMP ON THE KITCHEN TABLE.
teach.b: A Psalm says, "Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path." For a long time, that lamp sat in a church or a library. The press began to put it on kitchen tables.

how: Christians often give Bibles as gifts at baptisms, confirmations, weddings and graduations, and Bible societies print and give away Bibles in many languages.

games.q: you're a goldsmith with a new way to print. you could print anything at all. what do you choose for your great book?
o: a book of jokes that would sell fast.
the whole Bible, made to look like the finest handwritten copies.
a single page and nothing more.
games.why: Gutenberg printed the Latin Bible, laid out like the best handmade books, and many copies were finished by hand.

practice: Think of a book that changed something for you: maybe a Bible, a novel, or a book of poems someone handed you at the right time.

Then think of one person who might need a book right now, a friend, a child, a coworker, someone on your street, and choose a book for them. If you pray, pray for them as you choose; if you don't, just hold them in mind.
